Definition: from G1014; volition, i.e. (objectively) advice, or (by implication) purpose:--+ advise, counsel, will.
BiblicalUsage: Counsel is the word for purpose, will, resolve — God's and man's. In Acts 2:23 Jesus was delivered by the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God. In Acts 4:28 the rulers did whatsoever God's hand and counsel determined before to be done. In Ephesians 1:11 we are predestinated according to the purpose of him who worketh all things after the counsel of his own will. And in Hebrews 6:17 God, willing to show the immutability of his counsel, confirmed it by an oath.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the counsel of God is the anchor of my hope: what he determined before, he does, and his counsel cannot be broken by any counsel of men.
